hens_rule_text: Up to 6 hens or quail in total on parcels under 1 acre, no permit needed (in effect since March 4, 2022). Before 2022 poultry was only allowed on lots of 1 acre or more.
permit_notes: The city says no permit or fee is required. Enforcement is on a complaint basis.
setback_notes: Coop at least 30 ft from an adjacent dwelling, at least 5 ft from the side property line and 10 ft from the rear property line. Birds and coops may not be in front of the rear wall of the house.
coop_rules: At least 4 sq ft of coop space per bird, 8 sq ft of unpaved roaming area per bird, birds shut in the coop dusk to dawn, clean and predator-proof, food and water always available, electrical or heat sources must meet building code.
zoning_notes: The 6-bird limit applies to parcels under 1 acre; larger parcels fall under separate agricultural animal rules not checked here. Outdoor slaughter is not allowed. Fines up to $500 for first and second offenses, $1,200 after.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
